S: Lori Greene, a 32-year-old female, presents for a follow-up visit regarding her PTSD. She reports that she has been feeling better overall, with a decrease in the frequency of flashbacks and nightmares. She has been adhering to her current medication regimen without any difficulties. She denies any recent exacerbation of her symptoms. She also reports mild anxiety occasionally but manages well with relaxation techniques and support from her therapist.

O: Vital signs: BP 141/79, Wt 167 lb. Physical examination was unremarkable, with normal heart rate, respiratory rate, and temperature. No abnormalities noted in head, eyes, ears, nose, throat, or abdominal exams. Neurological exam showed no focal deficits, and cranial nerves were intact.

A: PTSD - improving. Lori’s current treatment regimen of sertraline 25 mg and prazosin 2 mg is effective, and she continues to benefit from cognitive-behavioral therapy. There have been no significant adverse effects reported. 

P: Continue current treatment with sertraline and prazosin. Encourage continued engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy.
